supervisor.complete_task: answer is graded. Questions (how many/what is/list) need the answer. Commands (like/follow/send/delete/add/move/play...) must be called with NO answer at all.
spotify.show_song_library: Only songs saved directly in the song library (not album songs, not playlist songs). Paginate fully (page_limit max 20).
spotify.show_album_library: Albums in the album library; each album has song_ids. Album songs are NOT in the song library. Paginate fully.
spotify.show_playlist_library: Each playlist has song_ids and is_public. Paginate fully (page_limit max 20).
spotify.show_song: Per-song details (release_date, genre, artists, album, duration, play_count). PUBLIC: takes NO access_token (passing one is an error). List APIs (library/liked/playlist/recommendations) return summaries without these fields - call show_song per id (call_each, no token) before ranking or filtering on them. play_count/like_count here are global totals.
spotify.show_liked_songs: Songs I liked. Paginate fully. Liked is separate from the song library and from downloads.
spotify.show_song_reviews: Reviews of a song by all users; filter my own with user_email=<my email>. A review holds my star rating: update it (update_song_review) instead of creating a second one.
spotify.show_downloaded_songs: Songs I downloaded. Paginate fully. Check it before download_song so nothing is downloaded twice.
phone.search_contacts: Contacts carry first_name, last_name, phone_number, email and relationships (list of strings such as 'friend', 'coworker'; spelling varies). Paginate fully (page_limit max 20). Print the distinct relationship strings, then filter case-insensitively (contacts_with_relation). Use the contact email to find the person in venmo/spotify.
phone.send_text_message: Sends one message to one phone_number. The text must be exactly what the task asks for. If the task is a reply to someone, read their message first (search_text_messages) and apply any condition it states.
venmo.show_transactions: Transactions I sent AND received. Filters: user_email, direction, min_created_at, max_created_at, query, min_amount, max_amount. A bare date as max_created_at can cut off that whole day: fetch with fetch_all_pages and filter the DATE part of created_at in Python (in_dates). Each has sender and receiver (name, email), amount, private, created_at, like_count.
venmo.show_social_feed: Friends' transactions as shown to me. Paginate fully. Use this (not show_transactions) when the task says 'social feed'. Check sender/receiver emails against the people named in the task.
venmo.create_transaction: receiver_email is required (look it up; do not guess). private=True only when asked 'privately'. On insufficient balance retry with payment_card_id from show_payment_cards.
venmo.show_sent_payment_requests: status filter: pending/approved/denied. Paginate fully. Each request has the receiver email, amount, created_at.
file_system.show_directory: Lists paths under directory_path. Use recursive=True and entry_type='files' (or 'directories') to see everything. Paths only: call show_file for created_at/content. Print the full plan before moving or deleting.
file_system.move_file: source_file_path -> destination_file_path (full new path incl. file name). Pass retain_dates=True so created_at is kept. Rename = move to the same directory with a new name. The destination directory must exist (create_directory first).
simple_note.search_notes: Returns note summaries WITHOUT content. Call show_note(note_id) for the content. Paginate fully. To change a note use update_note; create a note only if none exists.
spotify.show_recommendations: Personalized song summaries; paginate fully. Items lack release_date/play_count: fetch show_song per id before filtering by year. Recommendations may include songs already in my library - follow the task wording on whether to exclude them.
spotify.show_following_artists: Artists I follow. Paginate fully. Before follow_artist, compare with this list and follow only artists not yet followed (a repeated follow errors). A song's artist ids are in show_song['artists'].
spotify.follow_artist: Follow one artist by artist_id. Fails if already followed: build the target ids, subtract show_following_artists, then call_each on the rest.
spotify.remove_song_from_library: Removes one song from the SONG library only; it stays in playlists and albums. To remove a song 'everywhere' also call remove_song_from_playlist per playlist containing it. Do not touch anything the task did not name.
spotify.update_song_review: Takes review_id (from show_song_reviews with user_email=<my email>) plus rating/title/text. Use it when I already reviewed the song; use review_song only if no review exists. Ratings are integers.
spotify.show_playlist: Playlist details; the playlist list API gives song_ids. For duration or release_date call show_song per id, sum in code, and convert units carefully (check the unit in the doc: seconds vs minutes).
spotify.show_artist: Public artist details (takes NO access_token). Use it to resolve an artist name from an artist_id.
venmo.show_received_payment_requests: Requests others sent TO me; status filter pending/approved/denied. Paginate fully. Each has the sender's email: match senders to the people the task names (phone contacts' relationships/emails) before approve_payment_request. Approve only pending ones.
venmo.approve_payment_request: Takes payment_request_id (+ optional payment_card_id). On insufficient balance retry with a payment_card_id from show_payment_cards. Approve each request once; re-read the pending list afterwards.
venmo.show_payment_cards: My payment cards (id, last_four, expiry). Use an id as payment_card_id for approve_payment_request / create_transaction when the balance is not enough.
file_system.compress_directory: compress_directory(directory_path, compressed_file_path, delete_directory=True|False, overwrite). One call makes the archive and, with delete_directory=True, removes the source - do NOT also call delete_directory or build the archive by hand. Do it for exactly the directories the task names.
file_system.show_file: Returns content plus created_at/updated_at. Bill/receipt files: print one whole file to see its layout (several numbers: subtotal, tax, total); use amounts_with_context(content) and take the number the task asks for. Decide a file's month/year from its name or created_at as the task implies and print both.
file_system.delete_directory: Deletes the directory with ALL sub-directories and files, irreversibly. List its content first and delete only the exact directories the task names, after any compress/copy/move step has succeeded.
phone.get_current_date_and_time: The app's own 'now'. Use it (not an assumed date) for 'today', 'yesterday', 'last N days', 'this month/year'. Take the date part ([:10]) and use date_range / in_dates / days_since from the helpers.
venmo.like_transaction: Likes ONE transaction by transaction_id. Liking the same one twice errors. For 'like all X' build the exact id list in Python first (sender or receiver email in the people set, date part in range), print it, then call_each. Never like anything outside that list.
venmo.create_transaction_comment: Takes transaction_id and comment (exact text from the task). One comment per transaction; apply it to exactly the same id list as the likes when the task asks for both.
venmo.remind_payment_request: Reminds ONE pending sent request (payment_request_id). Build the list from show_sent_payment_requests(status='pending'): receiver email in the named people, age = days between created_at date and today (>= N means N or more days). Remind each request once.
venmo.create_payment_request: Needs user_email (the person to charge), amount (float), description. One request per person with that person's own share. Skip people who already paid you (check show_transactions received) when the task says so. Do not request from yourself.
spotify.play_music: Pass AT MOST ONE of song_id, album_id, playlist_id, queue_position (two together is an error). To play one specific song call play_music(song_id=...); it is added to the queue and played. To play a whole album/playlist pass only its id.
spotify.show_song_queue: Queue in play order; find the current song's index by matching show_current_song()'s song_id (check the field names with peek). 'Played so far incl. the current one' = entries up to and including that index, de-duplicated by song_id.
spotify.show_current_song: The song playing now; has song_id and artist ids/names. For the artist's follower count call show_artist(artist_id) (public, no token) and read follower_count.
spotify.show_album: Public album details incl. song_ids (no access_token). To rank an album's songs by play_count call show_song per song id; least/most played = min/max of play_count, print the ties.
spotify.search_albums: Search by query (title text); results can include similar titles - compare the title exactly (norm_text) and use that album_id. Public, no access_token needed.
spotify.search_artists: Filters: query, genre, min_follower_count, max_follower_count, sort_by. Result items may be summaries: peek one raw record, and re-check the genre and follower count in Python on the final list before writing. Paginate fully.
spotify.download_song: Downloads ONE song_id. A song already downloaded errors: compute target ids minus show_downloaded_songs ids first (still_needed). Download exactly the songs the task describes, nothing else.
spotify.like_song: Likes ONE song_id; already-liked songs error. Target ids minus show_liked_songs ids (still_needed), then call_each. 'Songs of artists I follow' = songs whose artists list contains a followed artist id (show_song per id, or search_songs with artist_id).
spotify.review_song: Creates a NEW review (rating 1-5, integer). If my review of that song already exists (show_song_reviews with user_email=<my email>) use update_song_review instead. Only write songs whose current rating differs from the target; leave songs already at the target untouched.
spotify.remove_song_from_playlist: Needs playlist_id AND song_id: removes one song from ONE playlist. For 'remove from my playlists' loop over every playlist whose song_ids contain a matching song and call it once per (playlist, song) pair; print the pairs first.
spotify.add_to_queue: Adds a song_id, album_id or playlist_id to the END of the queue without playing (play_music plays now). Pass exactly one id argument per call; for many songs call once per song id.
spotify.show_song_privates: Per-user data for a song (e.g. whether I liked/downloaded/own it). Needs access_token + song_id. Prefer the list APIs (liked/downloaded/library) for whole sets; use this only for single checks.
phone.show_alarms: Lists my alarms (alarm_id, time 'HH:MM', enabled, label, repeat_days). Paginate fully. 'Disable the rest' = every alarm except the named one gets enabled=False via update_alarm, changing nothing else.
phone.update_alarm: Takes alarm_id and ONLY the fields to change (time 'HH:MM', enabled bool). Move a time with shift_clock(time, minutes). Send only the changed field so other fields stay as they are.
phone.search_text_messages: Messages sent/received (sender/receiver, message, created_at). Paginate fully. Filter by phone_number of the person; the newest message from them states the request. Read it fully before acting.
phone.show_contact_relationships: Distinct relationship strings in the contact book. Run once; a task word like 'parents' or 'siblings' may cover several strings (mother, father, sister, brother...). Use contacts_with_relation with all that fit.
simple_note.show_note: Returns the full note incl. content (markdown text, often with checklists/lines). search_notes gives titles only: find the note by exact title, then show_note(note_id) for the content.
simple_note.update_note: Send note_id plus ONLY the fields that change; when editing content, resend the whole content with just the wanted lines changed (keep every other line, blank line and ordering exactly), never title/tags/pinned unless asked.
file_system.create_file: Creates a file at file_path with content (string). Use it for exports: build the exact text first (make_csv for CSV), print it, create each file once. Path must start with ~/; create the directory first only if the task needs a new one.
